findings.reason: the deliverable must name where a same-lane model swap is recorded (a model-change field, or a schema note that `lane_changes` also carries same-lane model swaps), otherwise the node writes a mislabelled lane-change entry that the plan's own §40 forbids.
findings.text: §41 says "The run's `lane_changes` history (`reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1774`) gains one entry naming the refused model, the chosen model and the reason `model-capacity`", and its done-when (line 402) asserts "`lane_changes` carries one entry naming sol, luna and `model-capacity`"; but `lane_changes` entries are built for a backend move (`from_backend`/`to_backend` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1615`) and are folded into a lineage record whose `kind` is literally `"lane-change"` (line 1776), while §40 asserts "The lane never changes" and §41's swap keeps the lane (codex) and changes only the model. The entry therefore records a lane change that did not happen, and a later reader of the run's lineage sees a spurious move on a run that stayed on one lane

findings.reason: adding a timeout case tightens the done-when but does not change what the node builds or where it records the swap.
findings.text: the mechanism (line 388) names four fallback triggers ("When the ask holds, fails, times out, or names the refused or an undeclared model") but the done-when exercises only hold, raise and answer-sol (line 398), and both mutations (line 407) are about the swap and the event match; no case and no mutation exercises the timeout branch, so that path of the mechanism has no measure and a builder could omit it with the suite still green
